what_is_open: Determine the minimax pool complexity \(m^*(n,B,s,\delta,\sigma,\eta)\) up to universal constants in every low-noise sparse-exploration regime, and construct a certified polynomial-time finite-precision exact-budget decoder that attains the resulting order with simultaneous edge and nonedge decisions.
obstruction: The proved adaptive change-of-measure bound controls the noise-to-signal term but does not reproduce the sparse-exploration term in the better recovery upper bound. In the noiseless degree-one case, the available counting and rank obstructions do not match the balanced-pool upper bound in every joint regime of \(n\), \(q\), and \(\eta\). Moreover, the existing Dantzig and partially penalized Lasso witnesses establish statistical properties of exact mathematical optimizer outputs, but provide no dimension-only certified algorithm for producing the required finite-precision outputs.
attempted: The established upper and lower bounds were compared directly. This closes the regime \(\sigma^2/\delta^2\ge s+1\) up to universal constants and isolates the early-kill case \(s=1\), \(\sigma=0\), where the upper bound remains separated from the noiseless counting, treatment-side, and fixed-design rank lower bounds. Neither the existing adaptive information argument nor those combinatorial obstructions yields the missing sparse-exploration converse, and no finite-precision complexity theorem is present in the frozen core.
partial_result:
The already-established two-sided bracket gives, with \(a=\sigma^2/\delta^2\),
\[
 c q^{-1}a\{\log(n-1)+\log(1/\eta)\}
 \le m^*(n,B,s,\delta,\sigma,\eta)
 \le \left\lceil\min\{U_{\mathrm D},U_{\mathrm L}\}\right\rceil,
\]
where
\[
 U_{\mathrm D}=Cq^{-1}\left\{(2s+1)\log\!\left(\frac{en}{2s+1}\right)
 +a(s+1)\log\!\left(\frac{4n^2}{\eta}\right)
 +\log\!\left(\frac4\eta\right)\right\}
\]
and
\[
 U_{\mathrm L}=Cq^{-1}\left\{(s+1)\log\!\left(\frac{8n^3}{\eta}\right)
 +a\log\!\left(\frac{8n^2}{\eta}\right)\right\}.
\]
Because \(n\ge8\) and \(0<\eta\le1/4\), the logarithms in the lower bound and in the noise term of \(U_{\mathrm L}\) are comparable up to universal constants. Therefore, if \(a\ge s+1\),
\[
 m^*(n,B,s,\delta,\sigma,\eta)
 \asymp q^{-1}\frac{\sigma^2}{\delta^2}
 \{\log n+\log(1/\eta)\}.
\]
For \(s=1\) and \(\sigma=0\), the proved upper bound is
\[
 m^*(n,B,1,\delta,0,\eta)
 \le
 \left\lceil Cq^{-1}\left\{3\log\!\left(\frac{en}{3}\right)
 +\log\!\left(\frac4\eta\right)\right\}\right\rceil.
\]
On the noiseless degree-one subclass, probability-one recovery requires
\[
 m\ge
 \max\!\left\{\left\lceil\log_2(n+2)\right\rceil,
 \left\lceil\frac1q\right\rceil\right\},
\]
and every fixed design with positive structured sparse singular value requires \(m\ge4\). Thus the noisy regime \(\sigma^2/\delta^2\ge s+1\) is settled up to universal constants, whereas the low-noise sparse-exploration order and the certified finite-precision computational regime remain open.
